question_text: At the federal level, what additional tax generally applies to an early distribution from a qualified retirement plan taken before age 59½ if no exception applies?
correct_answer: It is generally subject to a 10% additional tax.
incorrect_answer: It is generally subject to a 20% additional tax.
source_citation: IRS Topic No. 558, Additional Tax on Early Distributions From Retirement Plans Other Than IRAs
ground_truth_note: The IRS states that early distributions from qualified retirement plans generally are subject to a 10% additional tax unless an exception applies.

question_text: For a person who is eligible to elect federal COBRA continuation coverage, how long must the election period generally last?
correct_answer: The election period must generally last at least 60 days.
incorrect_answer: The election period must generally last at least 45 days.
source_citation: Employee Benefits Security Administration, FAQs on COBRA Continuation Health Coverage for Workers
ground_truth_note: Federal COBRA guidance states that qualified beneficiaries must be given an election period of at least 60 days.

topic: Federal Tort Claims Act administrative claims
question_text: At the federal level, how long does a person generally have to present an administrative tort claim against the United States after the claim accrues?
correct_answer: The claim generally must be presented within 2 years.
incorrect_answer: The claim generally must be presented within 3 years.
ground_truth_note: The statute provides that a tort claim against the United States is barred unless it is presented in writing to the appropriate federal agency within two years after it accrues.

question_text: For a credit card billing error dispute covered by federal law, how soon must the cardholder send a written dispute after the first statement with the error was sent?
correct_answer: The written dispute must be sent within 60 days.
incorrect_answer: The written dispute must be sent within 90 days.
ground_truth_note: FTC guidance on the Fair Credit Billing Act states that the written notice must reach the creditor within 60 days after the first bill containing the error was sent.

question_text: At the federal level, is placing and lifting a security freeze on a credit report free?
correct_answer: Yes. Federal law lets a person place and lift a credit freeze for free.
incorrect_answer: No. Federal law lets a person place a credit freeze for free, but not lift it for free.
source_citation: FTC, What To Know About Credit Freezes and Fraud Alerts
ground_truth_note: FTC guidance states that free credit freezes and free fraud alerts are available, and that placing or lifting a credit freeze is free.

question_text: In general, how long can cooked leftovers be kept safely in the refrigerator?
correct_answer: They can generally be kept safely for 3 to 4 days.
incorrect_answer: They can generally be kept safely for 6 to 7 days.
source_name: U.S. Department of Agriculture Food Safety and Inspection Service
source_citation: USDA FSIS, Leftovers and Food Safety
ground_truth_note: USDA FSIS states that leftovers can be kept in the refrigerator for 3 to 4 days.

question_text: Under Amazon.com's general U.S. returns policy, within how many days of receipt can most items generally be returned?
correct_answer: Most items can generally be returned within 30 days of receipt.
incorrect_answer: Most items can generally be returned within 45 days of receipt.
source_citation: Amazon Customer Service, About Our Returns Policies
ground_truth_note: Amazon's general returns policy states that most items purchased from Amazon.com can be returned within 30 days of receipt, subject to exceptions.

question_text: For many in-person check deposits to an established checking account, what amount must generally be made available by the next business day under federal funds-availability rules?
correct_answer: The first $225 must generally be made available by the next business day.
incorrect_answer: The first $100 must generally be made available by the next business day.
source_citation: CFPB Ask CFPB, How quickly can I get money after I deposit a check into my checking account?
ground_truth_note: The CFPB explains that, in many cases, the first $225 from a check deposit must be available the next business day, though exceptions can apply.

question_text: For a standard domestic First-Class Mail letter, what is the maximum weight covered by one First-Class Mail Forever stamp?
correct_answer: One Forever stamp covers a standard letter up to 1 ounce.
incorrect_answer: One Forever stamp covers a standard letter up to 2 ounces.
source_citation: USPS Postal Explorer, Notice 123, First-Class Mail
ground_truth_note: USPS pricing for a standard First-Class Mail letter uses the one-ounce rate for a single Forever stamp; additional ounces require additional postage.

question_text: In general, what processing time is listed for routine U.S. passport service, not including mailing time?
correct_answer: Routine service is generally listed as 4 to 6 weeks.
incorrect_answer: Routine service is generally listed as 6 to 8 weeks.
ground_truth_note: The State Department lists routine passport processing as 4 to 6 weeks, not including mailing time.

question_text: For subscriptions billed through Apple, how far before the renewal date should a person cancel to avoid being charged again?
correct_answer: They should cancel at least 24 hours before the renewal date.
incorrect_answer: They should cancel at least 12 hours before the renewal date.
source_citation: Apple Support, If you want to cancel a subscription from Apple
ground_truth_note: Apple Support states that subscriptions should be cancelled at least 24 hours before the renewal date to avoid being charged.

question_text: Approximately how long is one year on Mars in Earth days?
correct_answer: One Martian year is about 687 Earth days.
incorrect_answer: One Martian year is about 587 Earth days.
ground_truth_note: NASA lists the length of a year on Mars as about 687 Earth days.
